narrative.overview:
Every surface repeats one formula: a crafted object (the gold folding screen in the hero, the real product in a rendered phone or browser window for each project) set on one flat colour, its name set very large in a single-weight Mincho, and a few facts in a plain sans beside it. Colour is spent in whole fields, never in gradients or tints: azurite for the hero, one flat ground per project, ink for the index and the AI section, lavender for the closing contact, cream paper for reading. The objects carry the only depth; the grounds stay flat.

Density is low at the top of each section and rises where the reading starts. Bands and heads are large-type posters; case-study sections and blog articles settle onto paper in a two-column reading layout, the heading or the product held beside the text. Hairline rules in ink or paper at 18 to 30 percent opacity divide lists and sections; there are no cards and no boxed panels.

Links are underlined text, and the underline is the interaction: it appears, moves further from the letters, or thickens on hover. Only the main way into a section is a filled button, and it is a near-square ink block.
keyCharacteristics: One flat colour per section, edge to edge; the section's ink flips to light on dark grounds.
Hina Mincho at 400 for names, headings, numerals and the closing links; Instrument Sans for everything else.
Real objects (Blender-rendered screen, phone frame, browser window) carry soft cast shadows; nothing else is lifted.
Hairline dividers and underlines instead of cards, chips or icons.
Gold appears only as a fitting: a 1-2px line marking a current or fixed state.

rules.name: The One Ground Rule
rules.body: A section is one flat colour, edge to edge. A project's colour belongs to that project everywhere it appears, and no section mixes two grounds.

rules.name: The Gold Is a Fitting Rule
rules.body: Gold is never a fill, a text colour or a ground. It is a 1-2px line marking state, and only on ink or paper; on the project blues it has no contrast, so the current state there is marked in full ink.

rules.name: The One Weight Display Rule
rules.body: The display face is always 400. Hierarchy in display type comes from size and tight leading, never from weight or italic.

rules.name: The Sentence Case Rule
rules.body: No uppercase, no tracked-out labels. Letter-spacing is only ever negative, on display sizes.

rules.name: The Beside Rule
rules.body: On wide screens, the thing being explained stays beside the reading: the case-study heading sticks at 24px, the article's phone sticks full height. Neither floats over the text.

rules.name: The Objects Only Rule
rules.body: Shadows belong to rendered or physical objects (phone, window, video, disc). Text, buttons, lists and sections never cast one.

dos: **Do** give every new section one flat ground from the palette, and give a new project its own ground and tone.
**Do** set names, headings, numerals and closing links in Hina Mincho at 400, large and tight (line-height under 1 at headline sizes).
**Do** show the real product in the phone or browser frame on the project's ground.
**Do** derive quiet text by mixing the current ink toward the current ground, and keep full Light Ink for small text on dark grounds.
**Do** use underlines as the link affordance and animate only their offset, thickness or colour, on `cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1)`.
**Do** keep a 44px target on buttons and on every link under a coarse pointer, and drop all transitions under reduced motion.
donts: **Don't** use gradients, tints or textures on grounds, except the hero's grain.
**Don't** use gold as a fill, text colour or on a blue ground.
**Don't** put shadows on text, buttons, lists or sections; only objects cast them.
**Don't** add cards, chips, pills or boxed panels; divide with hairlines.
**Don't** bold or italicise the display face, or let the browser synthesise either.
**Don't** add uppercase or letter-spaced labels, or a small invented label above a heading.
**Don't** use icon glyphs or icon fonts; draw the few marks needed (play, stop) in CSS.
